note: The open items the logic pages carry, shown on those pages only and never appended to data/gaps.json (plan 12.0); lands_on names screen ids, logic_tech for the Tech page, logic_access for the Access page, V for the client views.

items.item: to be decided: how each kind of change reaches plans by default (at the next refresh, or pushed now)
to be decided: the small-change margin values; whether a picture-moved update needs the client to accept it
to be decided: how many days a plan may fall behind before it must refresh (the 120-day limit is a stand-in)
to be decided: whether a hold is the default when a fund leaves the list, and when an exit (sell out) is ever advised (G12 on the board reads: not on the approved list, exit)
to be decided: any grouping beyond risk level and time to goal, and a ceiling on the number of client groups
to be decided: how many mixes, and whether a mix change ever moves existing units
to be decided: who sends a change when the principal officer cannot be reached
to be decided: whether the financial planning team reviews planning rows on L02 before they are sent
to be decided: where the list of allowed staff lives (M03, as decided on 7 Oct 2026, or the Staff and roles screen), and whether both panels use one sign-in, the same as the app's
to be decided: where the reasons clients read are kept, and who edits them ({I15} or the panel)
to be verified: what counts as "digitally signed" for the record of why a change was sent
to be verified: whether moving the score lines between risk levels needs the client's fresh confirmation before it applies
to be verified: the wording that tells clients how and when a plan is updated (the fixed-fee agreement, gap G06)
to be decided: the batches for each kind of push; a call task after every urgent update, or only for one not accepted after three days
to be decided: whether the Adviser, Call centre and Support roles read the live reasons in the panel, or as content in {I15}
to be decided: how often each rule set is reviewed, and whether the monthly market readings need the second person

to be decided: where the rule values live when the app runs: sent by the app to {I04} on every run, or held in {I04} as central values with a copy per client (7 Oct 2026 call); which system holds the saved copy of record

to be verified: whether {I04} can run a saved set of inputs as of a date, as a trial run, in a batch; whether a call works the plan out again or returns the stored result until a review; whether a review reads the central value of the day or the client's own copy
to be verified: whether a running SIP can be moved to another fund through {I02} in one step, and how a hold reaches a basket on {I03}
to be decided: whether a basket with only one fund is allowed, given the most-in-one-fund limit
to be decided: whether a change set for a later date can be edited before it goes live, or must be pulled back and drafted again; whether a first plan built in that window uses the new values
to be decided: whether approval waits until the checker has opened every trial run panel; a hard limit on a move in one investment type
to be decided: whether a fix carries its own explanation for clients, and a watch on complaints
to be verified: the list of records kept and how long to keep them, against the nine records on the Admin and CRM tab (brief H6); whether a saved first result is one of them
to be decided: how the principal officer is reached for an urgent request
to be decided: the rule for spreading an exit across financial years (not modelled)
to be verified: {I04}'s run time per plan, and how many runs it takes at once
to be verified: the real size of a saved copy and its PDF, once the plan JSON contract exists (W03)
to be verified: a fresh security check at the moment of sending, through {I14}
to be decided: what follows when an urgent hold has no second sign-off within two working days
to be decided: whether a SIP outside the app that the client reports counts as a running SIP for a hold
to be decided: whether a staff role may change an assumption for one client (the plan engine allows it; 7 Oct 2026 call), and with what record
to be decided: when the email about a house-view change goes: on the go-live date to every plan it will change, or to each client when their plan takes it up
to be decided: whether a sent change refreshes R12's sample plans from fixed sample inputs, or they stay hand-written (gap G08)
to be decided: what a saved first result shows once the assumptions behind it have moved, and whether the nudges keep quoting its numbers

to be verified: whether launch places orders in the app as the board's section E draws, or through a link that opens {I02} with the portfolio loaded (gap G10; 7 Oct 2026 call); what the app then knows about a running SIP
to be decided: what comes at launch and what follows later
to be verified: the field changes to L02 to L09 now in progress (7 Oct 2026 call), so these screens show the same rows
to be decided: the most in equity per risk level, and any other mix limit a change must pass
to be decided: whether the access write-up for Spinach also lists the app's tier gates
to be decided: session rules for staff: the idle timeout, one session at a time, how old the fresh security check may be
to be decided: whether giving someone a working role needs a second person (it is the one way around the two-person rule)
to be verified: whether a pushed update (a hold, an exit, a fix) reaches a client whose yearly confirmation is overdue (Q04 on the board blocks plan re-runs)
to be decided: what the plan engine does with an amount below a fund's minimum SIP
to be decided: which sent changes need Compliance to sign before sending, beyond assumptions and risk scores
to be decided: how a new version of the plan engine (the maths) is approved, tried on existing plans, and named as a reason on a client's update
